item.title: Maslow's Hierarchy of Text
item.description:
Zero: you can write text that fits in the character limit.

One: you can write text, all run-together, no more, no less. With nothing more than capitalization, there are already Things You Can Do to inflect your text in subtle ways; but hopefully, in the Year of our Lord 2024, you get the full power of Unicode™ and can use things like “smart” quotes and dashes — maybe even emoji or Zalgo text if you’re lucky. (You may think you can bold or italicize text with Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols, U+1D400 to U+1D7FF, but they’re an accessibility nightmare and I won’t stoop to them even for the bit.)

item.title: J the Hard FP Way
item.description:
The title snowclone makes less sense with each post, but basically, this is the guide I wish I had when learning J. (Previously: React/Redux, SQL selects, and d3.)

J’s Getting Started page warns, “J is not like other languages you know.” I was and am somewhat doubtful. I feel like weird programming languages’ tutorials always assume “you” have only ever written C or FORTRAN, but I know lots of weird Haskell trivia, I’ve spent hours golfing code in stack-based languages (sometimes even ones that I didn’t write), and I broadcast PyTorch operations for a living.
